title: Attorney General of California

context.text: California uses a top-two primary: on June 2, 2026 Rob Bonta (D) received 56.6% and Michael Gates (R) 37.9% (Marjorie Mikels, Green, 5.4%), so the two advance to the general election.
Bonta was appointed Attorney General by Gov. Gavin Newsom in 2021 and elected in 2022; his campaign emphasizes opposing federal actions while Gates argues the office should prioritize crime.

candidates.name: Rob Bonta
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary.

summary.text: Rob Bonta is the incumbent Democratic Attorney General, appointed in 2021 and elected in 2022, seeking a second full term. A former Alameda city councilmember and East Bay assemblymember, he has made lawsuits against the Trump administration a central focus; his office marked its 100th such suit on October 15, 2026.

background.text: Former Alameda City Council member and East Bay member of the California Assembly.
Appointed Attorney General by Gov. Gavin Newsom in 2021 and elected in 2022.

priorities.text: Continuity of his office's work on housing-construction enforcement, antitrust cases targeting price fixing, organized retail theft, fentanyl trafficking, red-flag measures against gun violence, and challenging federal funding conditions, as he described it in an interview.
Affordability: "we're really delivering on that," he said of lowering costs for families.

record.text: Filed the office's 100th lawsuit against the Trump administration on October 15, 2026, challenging ICE civil immigration enforcement at state courthouses.

Joined a coalition of 12 attorneys general and two governors on October 9, 2026 suing the U.S. Department of Labor over termination of more than $45 million in unemployment-insurance modernization grants.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website or candidate statement was found; his positions on the guide's fixed issues were not located as direct statements.

candidates.name: Michael Gates
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary.
candidates.currentRole: Former Huntington Beach city attorney; former U.S. Justice Department deputy assistant attorney general (2025)

summary.text: Michael Gates is the Republican nominee, a former Huntington Beach city attorney who served in 2025 as a deputy assistant U.S. attorney general. He says the Attorney General's office should prioritize crime and law enforcement rather than lawsuits against the Trump administration.

background.text: Husband and father of five, per his candidate statement.
City Attorney for Huntington Beach, where he says he created a city criminal prosecutor program.
Served in 2025 as a deputy assistant U.S. attorney general at the Justice Department before launching his campaign in January 2026.

priorities.text: Public safety, including enforcing Proposition 36 and prosecuting crimes.
Prosecuting fraud and corruption, protecting parents' rights, and supporting voter ID.

positions.summary: His candidate statement says he would enforce laws that keep boys out of girls' sports.
positions.quote: enforce laws that keep boys out of girls' sports

record.text: As Huntington Beach city attorney, authored or helped form the city's challenges to state-mandated home-building requirements and the state sanctuary law, and the city's effort to institute a voter ID requirement.
